summary.intent: Group three related pending todos (#5 encrypt share itemName, #8 route shared-folder writes through SDK, #9 remove redundant web seeding) into a single GSD Phase 48, with a P0 addition to fix the web-e2e regression introduced by PR #498 (SDK self-bootstrap clobbering fresher in-memory folderTree state).
summary.outcome: Phase 48 was planned, branched, and executed through 5 of 6 plans: REQ-1 (P0 regression fix) is CI-green after 4 dispatches; REQ-2 (seeder removal), REQ-3 (sharedFolderTree SDK + web routing), and REQ-4 API (encrypted itemName column + api:generate) are committed; REQ-4 web (48-06, ShareDialog ECIES wrap + lazy backfill) was just launched and is pending completion.

repo: web-e2e.yml only auto-triggers on push to main (via ci-e2e.yml); it also has workflow_dispatch with `ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`, enabling pre-merge branch testing via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh workflow run web-e2e.yml --ref <branch>`
ThrottlerModule rate limits are NODE_ENV-gated (app.module.ts:56,61): strict in development, relaxed in test — running e2e locally without NODE_ENV=test causes 429s that look like app bugs
TypeORM migrationsRun=true in app.module.ts means the API auto-applies migrations on boot; no manual migration step needed for e2e
check-api-client.sh enforces that api-client regeneration is committed atomically in the same commit as API changes (145-file commit for 48-05)
Bash is hard-blocked from .env files by a repo security PreToolUse hook — .env operations must be given to the user as `!` shell commands
commitlint blocks parentheses in commit subjects; markdownlint is enforced on .md files (but skips .planning/)
The `cipherbox` dev compose DB and the `cipherbox_test` e2e DB are separate; local e2e must target cipherbox_test
The bin-restore-after-reload spec uses the real Web3Auth DEVNET Core Kit login (not the TEST_LOGIN_SECRET bypass), making it sensitive to DEVNET latency and causing ~50% login flake rate locally
Playwright's reuseExistingServer is true when CI env var is unset, so locally it reuses running servers — requires explicit server teardown between sessions
The IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY is optional locally when NODE_ENV!=production; jwt-issuer.service.ts generates an ephemeral RS256 keypair

code.finding: isLoading was `!coreKitInitialized || isLoggingIn || isLoggingOut` — missing `|| (coreKitLoggedIn && !isAuthenticated)`. This created a restore-window gap: after reload, coreKitInitialized flips true before restoreSession sets isAuthenticated, so BinPage's auth guard `if (!isLoading && !isAuthenticated) navigate('/')` bounced /bin→/login→/files. The fix keeps isLoading true until the restore resolves.

loadFolder did an unconditional folderTree.set(), clobbering fresher in-memory state with stale IPNS snapshots. Fixed with sequence guard: `if (existing && existing.sequenceNumber >= result.sequenceNumber) return existing`.

loadBin's auto-repair published an empty bin (no expectedSequenceNumber) when resolve returned null, because the API's upsertFolderIpns unconditionally overwrites latestCid. A transient post-reload 404 (IPNS propagation lag) triggered this, destroying the real bin record. Fixed by removing the destructive publish: bounded retry (6×500ms), then return in-memory empty {entries:[], sequenceNumber:0} without publishing.

ThrottlerModule's resolve rate limits are conditionally relaxed when NODE_ENV === 'test'. Running web-e2e locally without this env causes 429s on the /ipns/resolve endpoint, manifesting as step-8 timeouts that look like post-restore rendering slowness.

folderChildrenRef and sequenceNumberRef were written by both the web hook and the SDK post-mutation, creating a dual-writer desync class. Fixed in 48-04: sharedFolder:updated subscription is now the sole writer; useSharedWriteOps calls client methods and reads nothing back.

New SharedFolderTree keyed by shareId (not ipnsName) — two shares with the same ipnsName stay isolated. set() clones folderKey/ipnsPrivateKey; delete()/clear() zero key material. Mirrors Phase 47's owned folderTree ownership model.

Additive nullable `item_name_encrypted bytea` column added to both shares AND share_invites tables. No data UPDATE (server is zero-knowledge, can't re-encrypt existing plaintext). Column is on share_invites because A3 decision included the invite flow — recipient-rewrapped ciphertext must land on the claimed Share.

workflow: Pull Playwright trace artifacts (not just CI logs) before hypothesizing: the trace revealed the page was on /files (not /bin) at failure, ruling out bin-data bugs entirely and pointing to a navigation bounce. Three wrong-hypothesis CI dispatches could have been avoided.

Always reproduce locally with CI-matching environment (NODE_ENV=test, correct DB) before burning CI cycles — local/CI env differences (throttle, DB name, JWT key) can make bugs appear or disappear entirely
Run executors sequentially on a single branch (not parallel worktrees) for unattended multi-plan execution — avoids concurrent-mutation conflicts and commit ordering chaos

Use the Workflow tool's parallel fan-out for the understand phase before complex fixes: mapping stack bring-up, loadBin semantics, and IPNS durability concurrently gave a complete picture before touching code
GSD branching_strategy:phase auto-creates a branch from HEAD; if planning commits already exist on a differently-named branch, verify history is intact after init before proceeding
The `check-api-client.sh` pre-commit hook enforces api-client regeneration; NestJS migrations should be run against the test DB before regenerating so the schema is consistent
